curriculum.title: Responses to the Gospel in Acts

core.big_idea: Acts presents hearing, faith, repentance, confession, and baptism within whole conversion narratives.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Apostolic mission: Gospel Response within the Jesus, Gospel, and Discipleship cycle

claims.statement: The principal passage contains the textual evidence central to Responses to the Gospel in Acts.
Acts presents hearing, faith, repentance, confession, and baptism within whole conversion narratives.

core.interpretation_skill: Locate on timeline; read immediate context; identify genre; separate observation and application

learning.foundation_objective: Explain from the passage that acts presents hearing, faith, repentance, confession, and baptism within whole conversion narratives and locate the lesson on the whole-Bible timeline.
learning.extension_objective: Identify the immediate context and genre, then distinguish what the text directly states from a reasonable inference and application.
know: Acts presents hearing, faith, repentance, confession, and baptism within whole conversion narratives.
The lesson belongs in Apostolic mission.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, framework position, and application.
practise: Retell or analyse the passage using evidence from the text.
Name one faithful response without claiming more than the passage supports.
become: A learner who responds to Scripture with trust, wisdom, worship, service, repentance, or love as appropriate.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

say: The principal passage contains the textual evidence central to Responses to the Gospel in Acts.

ask: What does the text directly say?
What conclusion requires interpretation or synthesis?
zero_prep_card.do: Complete Responses to the Gospel in Acts Evidence Grid.
zero_prep_card.close: Restate the big idea, name one faithful response, and pray.
materials: Responses to the Gospel in Acts Evidence Grid

preparation.passage_context: Apostolic mission: Gospel Response within the Jesus, Gospel, and Discipleship cycle
text_observations: The principal passage contains the textual evidence central to Responses to the Gospel in Acts.

interpretation_notes: Start with the selected passage before moving to synthesis or application.
Read this as Narrative history and account for its immediate literary setting.
Distinguish explicit text, synthesis, inference, framework position, and prudential application.
theological_guardrails: Compare complete Acts narratives rather than extracting a rigid formula from one verse.
Clearly distinguish direct narrative observations from the curriculum’s synthesis of conversion response.

activities.title: Read and Notice: Responses to the Gospel in Acts
materials: Prayer, Wealth, and Trust Evidence Grid
steps: Read or retell Acts 2:36-41; 8:26-39; 16:25-34 in context.
Name two details the text directly states.
Restate the big idea in your own words.
activities.learning_link: Makes evidence classification and formation visible.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Draw the categories on blank paper or complete verbally.

activities.title: Responses to the Gospel in Acts Evidence Grid
steps: Sort statements into observation, interpretation/synthesis, and response.
Check each conclusion against the passage.
Name one limit or caution that prevents overclaiming.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank God for what the passage shows and ask for wisdom to respond faithfully.
closing.take_home_line: Acts presents hearing, faith, repentance, confession, and baptism within whole conversion narratives.

family.title: Family Bible Time: Responses to the Gospel in Acts
family.parent_intro: In about 15 minutes, read Acts 2:36-41; 8:26-39; 16:25-34 and explore this big idea: Acts presents hearing, faith, repentance, confession, and baptism within whole conversion narratives.

flow.instructions: Recall where Responses to the Gospel in Acts fits in the Bible story.
Read or retell Acts 2:36-41; 8:26-39; 16:25-34 and notice two details.
Ask what the passage directly says and what meaning follows from it.
Use the Responses to the Gospel in Acts Evidence Grid orally or on paper.
Choose one voluntary response and pray together.

questions: What happened or what was taught?
What does this show us about God, Jesus, or faithful life?
What is one response we can practise?

interactive.title: Responses to the Gospel in Acts Evidence Grid
interactive.instructions: Use the companion resource to sort direct observations from interpretations and responses.

family.weekly_action: Choose one concrete response connected to this lesson and practise it this week.
family.prayer: Thank God for what is clear in the passage; ask for wisdom to respond faithfully without claiming more than the text supports.
family.parent_note: Questions are welcome. Do not force disclosure, certainty, public prayer, baptism, or another public religious decision.

quiz.question: Which passage is central to Responses to the Gospel in Acts?
quiz.explanation: The lesson is governed by its principal passage.

quiz.question: Which reading habit is most responsible?
options: Observe context and genre before concluding.
Start with the application you want.
Treat every narrative detail as a command.

answer.text: Observe context and genre before concluding.

quiz.explanation: Observation and context precede synthesis and application.

quiz.question: Acts presents hearing, faith, repentance, confession, and baptism within whole conversion narratives.
quiz.explanation: This is the governed big idea for the lesson.

quiz.question: Should an inference be described as explicit text when the passage does not state it directly?
quiz.explanation: Inference and direct wording must remain distinct.

accessibility.reading_level: Upper-primary guided reading with concrete supports
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, abuse, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Use the lesson guardrails in the review sheet; answer from the evidence, avoid coercion, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
